title: Mother's encouragement and urging to leave the small town
summary: His mother told him to do what he wanted and wanted all her children out of Beardstown; the brothers left for college and never came back to live.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But I -- I really had a wonderful mother. She -- when my older brother used to rant and rave about me being a musician and all, she'd say, 'Well you gotta do what you gotta do. That's what you want to do, you do it.'
Yeah.
You don't have to --
She was very understanding?
Oh, yeah. She was at us -- tried to get us out of that small town. She said, you've got to get out of here.
Oh, she did?
Oh, yeah. You can't -- you'll never -- you'll never be happy, you'll deteriorate in a small town like --
And yet that meant she was going to lose you in a sense, all of you. If you all left?
Yeah, we all did.
Well --
My brothers left high school and went right to college. They never came back to live there --
They never came back?
-- they came back to visit -- and she'd go and visit them --
Yeah. What about Portia, did she leave?
Well she came back and taught school there for awhile, but after my --
Yeah.
-- father died and they sold my -- we also owned a house downtown in Beardstown, down on the Square --
Yeah?
And which when we had the other place, where I grew up, we rented to a doctor --
Yeah?
-- and so my father died, we finally got her -- my sister got her to sell the big place, it was too much --
Yeah?
-- and so the doctor we got him to leave and he went to someplace, another building and so they went there at that time and she enjoyed it there --
